description: Use this after uploading CAD files and before quoting, when the user asks whether a part can be made, wants a DFM (design for manufacturing) review, or asks what to change. Sends each uploaded file to the design check of a shop that makes its process (CNC machining, sheet metal, injection molding, wire harness) and returns ok, blockers and warnings per file plus ready_to_quote. The user's CAD file goes to that outside shop. Nothing is sent to a shop until the part's requirements are met. Fix blockers before calling get_quotes. Requires a Maglev API key.

file_ids.description: file_id values returned by the upload commands from upload_cad_for_quote

options.description: Per-file options: { file_id: { material, finish, tolerance, accept } }. material is required for CNC, sheet metal and molding and must be a value the shop lists, where it publishes a list. finish and tolerance are stated, or filled by accept: ["shop_standard"]. A response with readiness requires_input lists each missing field and its allowed values; fill them and call again. Ask the user for the material; never choose one for them. When a part is requires_input with its own requirements met, read suppliers[].requirements: they say what each supplier needs before it is asked. A part stays ready while one supplier can be asked: suppliers_dropped lists each supplier left out, with a code (cannot_be_told, not_offered, needs_input or unreachable), the field and the country it ships from (ships_from, null when not known), and how_to_fix says what would bring it in. Also accepted per file: quantity, speed, and for molding wall_mm and draft_deg.

processes.description: Optional per-file process override: { file_id: process }

name: check_manufacturability
title: Check manufacturability (DFM)
